subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should browser CSRF resistance for `admin-http-rpc` remain a centralized Gateway plugin-route Origin contract, or should this administrative endpoint additionally require a route-specific anti-CSRF token?
rationale: Source ownership points away from ACP, while current documentation claims centralized Origin protection; only security owners can confirm whether that contract is sufficient for intentionally unauthenticated and trusted-proxy deployments or whether a stronger protocol is required.

options.title: Prove and enforce the centralized guard
options.body: Verify that every supported auth mode rejects unapproved browser origins before plugin dispatch, repair the shared guard if needed, and add the full regression matrix.

options.title: Add route-specific CSRF tokens
options.body: Introduce a nonce or double-submit-token contract for administrative mutations, accepting additional client, documentation, and upgrade complexity.

options.title: Constrain unsafe auth modes
options.body: Disallow or explicitly narrow `admin-http-rpc` under `auth.mode=none` or browser-cookie trusted-proxy deployments when a safe provenance guarantee cannot be established.

recommendation.title: Prove and enforce the centralized guard
recommendation.body: Verify that every supported auth mode rejects unapproved browser origins before plugin dispatch, repair the shared guard if needed, and add the full regression matrix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on Gateway-authenticated plugin HTTP route boundaries makes this the strongest available code-history routing candidate for the shared security contract.
